findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, so codes can be reused
findings.body: Each request decrypts and validates a snapshot of the full backup-code array, then writes a newly encrypted replacement array. Two concurrent credential requests using the same code can both pass the check before either update commits and both receive sessions. Requests using two different codes can also overwrite each other's stale array and restore a code that the other request consumed. Recovery codes are documented as one-time credentials, so consumption needs a transaction/row lock or a conditional update-and-retry that ensures the stored value has not changed before issuing the session.

findings.title: Backup codes cannot be used for OAuth/SAML two-factor recovery
findings.body: The external identity-provider guard rejects every credentials request that lacks `totpCode` before the backup-code branch at line 131 is reached. A backup code is intended to replace the TOTP code, so it necessarily has no `totpCode` and receives `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` instead. The external TOTP login page also selects `ExternalTotpFooter`, which provides no Lost access option. Consequently, users whose Google/SAML account has 2FA enabled cannot recover with the backup codes generated by this feature. Treat a backup code as a valid second-factor input in the external-provider and password-routing guards, and expose the backup-code choice in that login flow.

findings.title: Dismissing the backup-code dialog leaves settings state reporting 2FA as disabled
findings.body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, this only changes the modal step; `onEnable()` is deferred until the custom Close button at line 269. Normal Dialog dismissal is still wired directly through `onOpenChange` at line 166, so closing with Escape, the dialog close control, or an outside dismissal can close the modal without notifying the parent that the server has already enabled 2FA. The settings switch/local state can then remain unchecked, and attempting to enable again returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` until the page is refreshed. Route successful-dialog dismissal through the same completion handler or prevent dismissal until the explicit completion action.

findings.title: The setup password visibility toggle cannot reveal the password
findings.body: This new `PasswordField` call passes `type="password"`. `PasswordField` spreads its props after its internally computed visible/hidden `type`, so the supplied prop always overwrites the computed `type="text"` when the eye button is clicked. The control advertises Show password but remains masked. Remove the explicit type here or change PasswordField so its visibility state takes precedence.

findings.title: The backup-code authentication and one-time-use paths have no automated coverage
findings.body: The added e2e coverage only opens the backup-code screen and checks that download/copy controls exist; it never reads a generated code, logs in with it, verifies that it is consumed, or disables 2FA with it. These are the feature's security-critical server paths, and the file explicitly leaves them as TODOs. Add integration/e2e coverage for successful backup-code login, rejection on reuse, and backup-code-based disablement.
